Crop: tomato
Disease: Late blight
Scientific name: Phytophthora infestans
Symptoms: Water-soaked irregular patches on leaves; Patches become dark brown or black; White fungal-like growth may appear on leaf undersides in humid conditions; Infection may spread to stems and fruits
Early signs: Pale green water-soaked patches on leaves
Low-cost actions: Use healthy seedlings; Remove and destroy infected plants; Avoid unnecessary irrigation during disease development
Chemical options: 
Favorable conditions: Low temperature around 12-15 degrees Celsius; Relative humidity above 96%; Cloudy humid weather and light rain

Crop: tomato
Disease: Leaf mold
Scientific name: Passalora fulva
Symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots develop on upper leaf surfaces; Olive-green to brown velvety growth appears underneath leaves; Spots may merge into larger affected areas; Leaves gradually yellow, dry and fall; Severe infection can cause extensive defoliation
Early signs: Small pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces; Early olive-green growth on the lower leaf surface
Low-cost actions: Improve air circulation between plants; Remove severely infected lower leaves; Remove infected crop debris; Avoid excessive leaf wetness; Maintain adequate spacing between plants
Chemical options: 
Favorable conditions: Relative humidity above 85%; Moderate temperatures; Prolonged moisture on leaves

safety.disclaimer: Weather indicators do not confirm disease infection. NASA POWER provides gridded weather estimates. The configured Dhaka coordinates may not represent the farmer's actual field. Consult an agricultural officer when symptoms or uncertainty are present.
